title: Requirements, Scope & User Experience
description: Translate an idea into observable requirements, user journeys, constraints, acceptance criteria, and a small implementable MVP.

lessons.title: Problem statements
lessons.principle: A problem statement identifies who struggles, under which conditions, and what improvement matters.
lessons.practice: Write a two-sentence problem statement without presupposing a framework or AI solution.

lessons.title: Distinguish needs from features
lessons.principle: 'Users lose their place' describes a need; 'add a dashboard' is only one possible solution.
lessons.practice: Ask AI for three solution options and test them against the original user problem.

lessons.title: Stakeholders and users
lessons.principle: Different actors may have different permissions, goals, abilities, and workflows.
lessons.practice: Name primary users, administrators, operators, and people affected by the system.

lessons.title: Map permission-sensitive journeys
lessons.principle: A viewer and an editor may see the same screen but must not have identical write capabilities.
lessons.practice: Draw who can create, read, update, and delete each resource before designing screens.

lessons.title: User stories
lessons.principle: A user story records an actor, goal, and reason; it is not a substitute for a testable contract.
lessons.practice: Write 'As a learner, I can resume a lesson so that...' then add measurable conditions.

lessons.title: Turn stories into scenarios
lessons.principle: Given-When-Then scenarios describe observable success and failure.
lessons.practice: Include 'given no saved progress' and 'given a corrupted saved value' for resume behavior.

lessons.title: Functional requirements
lessons.principle: Functional requirements define observable system behaviors and input/output contracts.
lessons.practice: Specify actions, valid values, permissions, success states, and error states.

lessons.title: Reject vague requirements
lessons.principle: 'Fast and intuitive' needs observable thresholds or a user-testing method.
lessons.practice: Rewrite 'search works' as a query, matching rule, empty-state behavior, and expected response limit.

lessons.title: Nonfunctional requirements
lessons.principle: Performance, accessibility, reliability, privacy, security, and portability describe qualities of the whole solution.
lessons.practice: Give each important quality a measurable check and deployment context.

lessons.title: Set realistic quality targets
lessons.principle: Targets without user population, devices, or workloads can mislead optimization.
lessons.practice: State that a task page must work with keyboard-only navigation and under a chosen representative load.

lessons.title: Scope and MVP
lessons.principle: A minimum viable product tests a core value proposition with the smallest coherent feature set.
lessons.practice: Split features into essential, next, and optional categories.

lessons.title: Prevent scope expansion
lessons.principle: New AI-generated suggestions should not silently override the agreed MVP.
lessons.practice: Keep a deferred-features list and reject unrelated edits from the initial pull request.

lessons.title: User flows and states
lessons.principle: A screen needs navigation, loading, empty, success, error, and recovery behavior.
lessons.practice: Sketch the main path and one failed path before coding UI.

lessons.title: Design for interruption
lessons.principle: Network loss, double submission, stale sessions, and partial completion affect real journeys.
lessons.practice: For save-task, define pending feedback, retry behavior, and whether duplicate tasks are possible.

lessons.title: Data and privacy requirements
lessons.principle: Collecting personal data creates retention, permission, protection, and deletion obligations.
lessons.practice: List the minimum fields needed and why each must be stored.

lessons.title: Limit AI input exposure
lessons.principle: Prompts and attachments can transfer data outside the application boundary.
lessons.practice: Use synthetic examples for model requests and avoid pasting real credentials or private user records.

lessons.title: Acceptance criteria
lessons.principle: Acceptance criteria should make it possible for an independent person to decide whether a requirement is met.
lessons.practice: Write positive, negative, and boundary-case examples for each feature.

lessons.title: Define an executable oracle
lessons.principle: A test oracle is the independently specified expected output for given conditions.
lessons.practice: For an empty title, require a visible validation message and no new stored task.

lessons.title: Specification handoff
lessons.principle: A useful implementation brief joins scope, assumptions, interface, data, failure modes, and tests.
lessons.practice: Ask AI to identify ambiguous areas before asking it to code.

lessons.title: Freeze a bounded work order
lessons.principle: A good brief states in-scope files, out-of-scope systems, constraints, and acceptance checks.
lessons.practice: Review the generated plan against the brief before implementation and update it only for evidence-based changes.

codeExamples.snippet:
Feature: Create task
Scenario: Reject blank title
  Given the task list is open
  When I submit an empty title
  Then I see a required-field message
  And no task is saved

MVP: create and complete a task
Out of scope: sharing, AI summaries, payments
Constraints: mobile keyboard, offline recovery
Acceptance: create/reload/complete + empty-input test
